title: Maitreya
hookLine: the coming Buddha, honored in Theravada and Mahayana alike

cards: A Pali sutta tells a long, dark story about the world going downhill. People grow more violent. Theft spreads, then killing, then lying, and lives grow shorter and shorter.
Then, at the bottom, something turns. People look at one another and decide to stop killing. Lives lengthen again.
Slowly, the world grows good. And at that time, the Buddha says, another Buddha will arise, named Metteyya, teaching the same teaching he taught. Year two told this story.
Today, the one it points to.

teach.b: First, a shared figure. Maitreya is the Sanskrit name; in Pali, Metteyya. He's named in the Pali texts that Theravada Buddhists keep, and honored across the Mahayana too.
Schools differ on a great deal; here is one hope they hold in common. Second, where he waits.

Tradition says Maitreya now lives as a bodhisattva in the Tushita heaven, where, the stories say, the bodhisattva who became Gotama Buddha waited before his last birth. He isn't a Buddha yet. He's preparing.
Some statues show Maitreya seated with both feet on the ground, as if about to stand up and come.
And in China a wandering monk from the stories, round-bellied and laughing, a cloth sack over his shoulder, came to be seen as one of his forms. His name is Budai.
If you've seen a laughing figure at a restaurant door or a temple gate, you may have met him. Fourth, what a coming Buddha says about now. Look at the order in the Pali story.
The new Buddha doesn't arrive and repair a broken world.
They give up killing, decency returns one choice at a time, and only then does Metteyya arise. The future is built out of ordinary kindness, long before anyone shining appears.
Some Buddhists pray to meet Maitreya in a future life; others treat the hope as a reason to practice now. Either way, it doesn't ask anyone to sit and wait.

how: Buddhists in Theravada and Mahayana lands honor Maitreya as the Buddha to come; some dedicate merit in the hope of meeting him, and in China images of the laughing Budai stand at temple entrances.

o: the first disciple the Buddha taught after his awakening
the Buddha still to come, honored by Theravada and Mahayana
the heaven where a bodhisattva waits before his last birth

games.q: the one to come: tap the pairs.

s: he is named in the Pali texts as Metteyya and honored in Theravada and Mahayana alike.
tradition says he waits as a bodhisattva in the Tushita heaven.
in the Pali story, people turn back to kindness before the new Buddha arises
they give up killing first; then Metteyya arises.

games.q: the world has been sliding downhill for ages: more violence, shorter lives. in the Pali story, what turns it around?
o: people decide to stop killing, and decency returns
the new Buddha arrives and fixes everything
games.why: people turn first. only after the world has grown good again does Metteyya arise.

practice: Picture a morning some years from now in a place you know, your street, your kitchen, a school down the road, just a little kinder than today: someone holding a door, a neighbor checking in, a tired person waved ahead in line.
Let it get specific, with colors and voices, and notice one thing in it you could begin yourself. Then let the picture fade back into the breath.

wordCard.voice: Maitreya. In Pali, Metteyya: the Buddha still to come, honored in Theravada and Mahayana alike. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit; in Pali, Metteyya: the name of the Buddha who is still to come.

carryVoice: Your line: the one to come. In the old story, people turn first. Until tomorrow.
